title: Compliance, Data Protection, and Securing AI Workloads
bodyMarkdown:
## The shared responsibility model

Compliance on Google Cloud is **shared**. Google attests to the **security of the cloud** (infrastructure, physical, platform — covered by certifications like **SOC 2**, ISO 27001, PCI DSS). The customer is responsible for **security in the cloud**: their application, IAM, data handling, and operations. Google's SOC 2 report does **not** make your app SOC 2 compliant — you still pursue your own.

## Regulatory drivers and the controls that satisfy them

| Regime / data type | Key obligations | Typical Google Cloud controls |
|---|---|---|
| **HIPAA** (PHI) | Sign a **BAA**; use covered services; safeguards | CMEK, Data Access audit logs, least-privilege IAM, VPC-SC |
| **PCI DSS** (card data) | Protect/limit PANs; reduce scope | **Sensitive Data Protection** tokenization; segmentation; logging |
| **GDPR** (EU PII) | Data-subject rights; lawful processing; residency | **DPA**, `gcp.resourceLocations`, SDP discovery/classification |
| **Data sovereignty** | Data + access stay in-region | **Assured Workloads** (e.g., EU Regions and Support), org policy |
| **Children's privacy** | Limit collection; parental controls | Data minimization, SDP, strict access |

## Sensitive Data Protection (formerly Cloud DLP)

A managed service to **discover, classify, and de-identify** sensitive data (PII, PANs, secrets) across BigQuery, Cloud Storage, and streamed content.

- **De-identification:** masking, bucketing, and **tokenization** — including **format-preserving** and **deterministic** methods that keep referential integrity for analytics joins while removing live data. This is the recommended way to **reduce PCI scope** for PANs.
- **Discovery:** profile where sensitive data lives to support GDPR access/erasure requests and data-governance.

## Data residency and sovereignty

- **Assured Workloads** enforces residency and **personnel/support access** restrictions per control package (e.g., EU Regions and Support).
- Pair with `constraints/gcp.resourceLocations` so resources cannot be created outside approved regions.
- A single EU multi-region bucket addresses one storage location only — not org-wide enforcement or personnel access.

## Securing AI workloads

Generative AI introduces new attack surfaces: prompt injection, jailbreaks, unsafe content, and **sensitive-data leakage** in responses.

- **Model Armor** screens **prompts and responses** for prompt injection, jailbreak attempts, and unsafe content, and integrates with **Sensitive Data Protection** to detect/de-identify sensitive data in the flow.
- **Secure model deployment:** put Vertex AI projects behind **VPC-SC**, use least-privilege IAM and CMEK, and govern model/container provenance with **Binary Authorization** where applicable.
- Note the layering: **Cloud Armor** protects the web layer (DDoS, common exploits) but does **not** understand prompt semantics — Model Armor does.

## Audits and evidence

Compliance demands **evidence**: enable the right **Cloud Audit Logs** (Data Access for PHI/PII), export to an immutable, restricted destination, and use **Security Command Center** to track posture and findings over time.
